# Lab 3.10: BigQuery Storage Read API

## What We Are Going to Do
Read a table directly with the Storage Read API, in parallel streams, selecting only some columns and rows.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Install the libraries.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">pip install --quiet google-cloud-bigquery-storage pyarrow pandas</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Create a read session.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">cat &gt; read_api.py &lt;&lt;'EOF'
import os
from google.cloud.bigquery_storage import BigQueryReadClient, types

client = BigQueryReadClient()
table = "projects/bigquery-public-data/datasets/usa_names/tables/usa_1910_current"
session = client.create_read_session(
    parent=f"projects/{os.environ['PROJECT_ID']}",
    read_session=types.ReadSession(
        table=table,
        data_format=types.DataFormat.ARROW,
        read_options=types.ReadSession.TableReadOptions(
            selected_fields=["name", "number", "year"],
            row_restriction='state = "WA" AND year &gt;= 2015'),
    ),
    max_stream_count=4,
)
print("Streams opened:", len(session.streams))
frames = [client.read_rows(s.name).to_dataframe(session) for s in session.streams]
import pandas as pd
df = pd.concat(frames)
print(df.shape)
print(df.groupby("year")["number"].sum())
EOF
python3 read_api.py</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[Console] Notice what is not there.** Open **Personal history**. There is **no query job**. The Read API reads storage directly and is billed by bytes read, not by a query.

4. **[CLI] Use it through the normal client.** The BigQuery client uses the Read API automatically for large results:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">python3 -c "
from google.cloud import bigquery
c = bigquery.Client()
df = c.list_rows('bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare', max_results=50000).to_dataframe()
print(df.shape)"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Streams | Up to 4 parallel streams |
| Column/row filters | Applied on the server |
| Format | Apache Arrow |
| Billing | Read API bytes, no query job |
